# An account kept to a finer unit than its currency has.
#
# GnuCash stores a smallest unit per account, not only per commodity, and this
# one is set to thousandths. Fuel is the everyday reason: 1.819 a litre is a
# tenth of a cent, and a book tracking it needs the third decimal even though
# a Canadian dollar has two.
#
# What this fixture produces: `commodity_scu: 1000` on the account, and the
# amounts below round-tripping exactly —
#
#   Expenses:Fuel 18.190 CAD
#   Assets:Bank  -18.190 CAD
#
# Validating or writing those against the *currency's* hundredths instead
# would refuse 18.190 as an amount CAD cannot hold, and round it away on
# export — on an account that holds it perfectly well.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_account_scu.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	commodity_scu: 1000
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Fuel
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	commodity_scu: 1000

2026-02-01 * "10 litres at 1.819"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Expenses:Fuel 18.190 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank -18.190 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
